x: Some months ago Jack confided to the writer that he had been inspired and encouraged throughout his long career in athletics by the thought of some of our earlier Belgrave enthusiasts - men like Parker, Belchamber and Horwood - who had impressed him in those early 1920 days with their love of the sport and their Club.

Lord Parker, of New Malden, to whom much of the credit for the Belgrave Harriers' progress goes, was awarded his peerage in the Peace Honours List 'for distinguished services to Amateur Athletics and the public'.
The Captain that day was Bert Footer and the rest of the team were Allum, Carter, Flower, Ginty, Parker, Patience; Shaw, Ring, Rice, Shields and Taylor.
